questions: What constitutes an 'invalid temperature entry' that should be excluded? For example, should NaN, None, non-numeric strings, or out-of-range values be dropped, and if so, how (drop entire row, fill with something)?
How should the heatmap handle duplicate entries for the same (Month, Day) combination? Should it take the mean, last, first, or raise an error?
Should the 'Time' column be used at all, or is it only required for validation? If used, how should it affect the heatmap (e.g., aggregate temperatures across times for each day)?
What should happen if the DataFrame has dates that span multiple years? Should the heatmap aggregate across years, treat each year separately, or raise an error?
Should the heatmap's axes (Month, Day) be sorted in a specific order (e.g., chronological month 1-12, day 1-31) or follow the data order?
What is the expected behavior if some days in a month are missing? Should the heatmap show NaN/blank for those cells, or interpolate/fill with a default?
Should the function set any specific heatmap parameters (e.g., colormap, color range, annotation, figure size) beyond the title?
Is the function expected to close or show the plot, or just return the axes object without displaying?
